No. The evidence shows tree-cover loss on only a small part of the property in 2021.

- Hansen data mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021, roughly 2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha asset. A further 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as an event.
- The loss is corroborated. Later years were observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area.
- Most of the affected area (68.1 ha) is mapped as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). Another 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest, and none is native forest.

The data does not show whether this was deforestation or land-use change. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation. The data also does not establish the cause, the legality, who was responsible, or any compliance status.
